# Adoption measurement, monthly update and roadmap

**Owner:** AI Engineering — business engagement
**Dashboard:** `reports/adoption_dashboard.html` (regenerated by every pipeline run)
**Computed by:** `src/retail_pipeline/adoption.py` — the definitions below and the
code are the same definitions; if one changes the other must.

---

## Part 1 — Measurement plan

### Why measure at all

The steering group will ask "is anyone using it" at the first review. "I think
so" is not an answer, and neither is a number nobody can define. Everything below
is fixed in code so that the figure reported in month 6 means what the figure in
month 1 meant.

### Definitions

| Metric | Definition | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| **Reach** | Distinct users with ≥1 event in the last 4 weeks ÷ licensed users | Did it get into people's hands? |
| **Activation** | Users who have ever acted on a recommendation ÷ licensed users | Did it change what anyone did? |
| **Action rate** | `apply` events ÷ `view` events | Was it useful *per look*? |
| **Stickiness** | Weekly active ÷ monthly active | Habit or novelty? |
| **CSAT** | Mean of 1–5 in-report feedback scores | How does it feel to use? |
| **Depth** | Sessions per active user per week (30-min session gap) | Casual or working tool? |

**Activation is the one that matters.** A view changes nothing. Reach is easy to
move with an email; activation is not.

**Action rate is deliberately a ratio of events, not of people**, so it stays
comparable as the user base grows. Reach going up will usually push action rate
*down* — new users act less — and a measure that punishes you for onboarding
people is a measure that will get gamed.

### Instrumentation

| Event | Source in production |
|---|---|
| `view` | Power BI / Fabric report usage metrics |
| `apply` | Merchandising tool audit log — a recommendation accepted onto a planogram or bundle |
| `export` | Report export log |
| `feedback` | In-report feedback button → SharePoint list |

> The event log in this repository is generated by `scripts/simulate_usage.py`
> because the solution has not been deployed to real users. The schema is the
> production schema and the metrics are computed for real from it; swapping in a
> real extract is a one-line config change. This is stated here, in the code, and
> in the README, because an adoption number of unclear provenance is worse than
> no adoption number.

### Reporting cadence

| Who | What | When |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery team | Full dashboard | Weekly |
| Business Engagement Lead | Dashboard + narrative | Fortnightly |
| Steering group | One page: headline four, trend, one decision | Monthly |
| Team leads | Their own team's cut | Monthly |

Every team gets its own number, because an aggregate hides exactly the thing
worth acting on. This quarter the aggregate is on target and one team is at 50%.

## Part 2 — Monthly update (June 2026)

*Sent to: Merchandising, Category Management, Online Trading, Marketing, Store Ops,
Data & AI. 300 words, because a 900-word update is not read.*

---

**Frequently Bought Together — month 3**

Twelve weeks since launch. Headlines:

- **76% of you have used it in the last four weeks** — above our 70% target.
- **77% have acted on at least one recommendation.** That is the number we
  actually care about; a view changes nothing.
- **Feedback sits at 4.18 out of 5** across 62 responses.
- **Action rate is 22.6% against a 25% target** — the one measure below target,
  and the honest reason is that it fell as more people came on. New users
  browse before they act. We expect it to recover; if it hasn't by August we
  will say so here rather than quietly retire the target.

**What we learned this month.** The two workshops did more than any email:
weekly reach went from 19% to 42% after the first and from 36% to 47% after the
second, and both held. We are running a third in July.

**Where it isn't working.** Store Ops is at 50% reach and 3.4 on feedback — the
only team below both targets. The comments are clear that the view is built
around catalogue decisions that team doesn't make. That is a fit problem and
another training session won't fix it. We are meeting the Store Ops lead in July
to decide between a store-level view and taking them out of scope. We would
rather report a smaller honest number than a larger diluted one.

**Next.** A/B test design for the incremental-revenue question, a July workshop,
and the category-hierarchy filter that four of you have now asked for.

Questions, or want a walkthrough for your team — just reply.

## Part 3 — Roadmap

| When | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Jul 2026** | A/B test design — one category, four weeks, on vs off | The only defensible route to an incremental-revenue number. Everything else is correlation |
| **Jul 2026** | Store Ops decision — adapt the view or descope | A target nobody owns is not a target |
| **Aug 2026** | Category hierarchy in the product dimension | Four teams have asked; every conversation reaches it within five minutes |
| **Aug 2026** | Tune `min_support_count` against observed action rate | Currently 30 baskets by judgement. Action-rate-per-rule turns that into evidence |
| **Q4 2026** | Rolling-window vs all-history comparison | Seasonality. Needs the A/B harness to be measurable |
| **Q4 2026** | Customer-level personalisation — decision point, not commitment | Only worth revisiting if the identifier coverage problem is solved |

**Not on the roadmap, and why:** automated pricing or promotion actions. Every
review someone asks. The answer stays no until we can attribute revenue to a
recommendation, and that starts with the A/B test.

## Part 4 — Executive one-pager

**Frequently Bought Together** — ranked product affinities for the full
catalogue, published nightly into the merchandising report.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | Delivered, in adoption |
| **Investment** | One engineer, three weeks, existing infrastructure, no new licences |
| **Coverage** | 99.9% of the 3,803-line catalogue |
| **Evidence base** | 522,566 clean transaction lines, 19,773 baskets, 3.6% of source data rejected by automated quality rules |
| **Reach** | 75.8% of 62 licensed users (target 70%) |
| **Activation** | 77.4% have acted on a recommendation |
| **Satisfaction** | 4.18 / 5 |

**The one thing to know:** adoption is ahead of target and the tool is trusted,
but we cannot yet put a revenue number against it. Attribution needs a controlled
test, and inventing a number we cannot defend would cost more credibility than it
would buy.

**Decision requested:** approve a four-week A/B test in one category.

**Risk being managed:** one of five teams (Store Ops) sits well below target
because the solution does not fit how they work. Being resolved in July by
adapting the view or removing them from scope — not by more training.
